newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - June 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - June 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- APPLE DAILY -- The former chief of Xinhua News Agency in Hong Kong, Xu Jiatun, warned that if the Chinese Communist Party remained in Hong Kong after the handover, it should register with the Special Administrative Region. Otherwise, it would be illegal and embarrass Hong Kong Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa.

-- MING PAO -- Taiwan will set new visa regulations for Hong Kong people after the handover, who will be treated as foreigners and liable to be forced to leave if they are involved in activities not listed on their visa applications.

-- Six people in Beijing were detained for publishing a novel which reveals the inside story of the suicide of the former vice-mayor of Beijing, Wang Baosen, and the corruption among senior cadres and their children.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- China Telecom (Hong Kong), which will be listed in Hong Kong within the year, will have mobile phone businesses in several Chinese provinces, and its total assets will be comparable to total assets of "15 to 20" H-share firms.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Of 1,200 Hong Kong teachers tested on their Mandarin Chinese recently, only a dozen could meet the mainland teaching standard.

-- WEN WEI PO -- The deputy chief of the Beijing Science Academy said a prosperous and stable Hong Kong after the handover would bring opportunities for scientific and technological cooperation between China and the territory.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese Premier Li Peng inspected Sichuan province. He said 50 million poor people in China could have enough to eat and wear by the end of the century, and the key lay in developing technology and education.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The People's Liberation Army's investment vehicle was injecting HK$490 million worth of assets into its Hong Kong-listed arm Continental Mariner Investment.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen said Hong Kong would be China's bridge to the world after the handover.
-- A survey had revealed that directors at many small banks were keeping an increasingly large slice of attributable profits for themselves compared with their larger rivals.
